best_architecture: Recommended pattern: a single long-lived MCP client manager that owns the server subprocess and one persistent ClientSession, driven from a dedicated, single-owner asyncio task. Core design decisions: (1) Single owning task for the session lifecycle. The mcp SDK is built on anyio, and stdio_client() + ClientSession both open anyio cancel scopes / task groups internally. AnyIO requires that a cancel scope be entered and exited in the SAME task. The dominant production failure ('RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in') comes from spawning the session in one task and closing it (or the AsyncExitStack) in another. So the client should run its connect/serve/teardown loop inside ONE long-lived asyncio.Task (or anyio task group), and other coroutines submit tool-call requests to it via an asyncio.Queue / Future-resolution mechanism rather than touching the session object directly. The hermes-agent design ('each MCP server runs as a long-lived asyncio Task on a dedicated background event loop, keeping its transport context alive') is the canonical reference for this. (2) Reuse one persistent session, do NOT reconnect per call. Per-call reconnection pays subprocess spawn + initialize() handshake latency every time and is the slow, fragile path; keep the session open for the orchestrator's lifetime and multiplex calls over it (call_tool is async and the SDK matches responses to requests by JSON-RPC id, so concurrent in-flight calls over one session are supported). Treat 'connection pooling' for stdio as 'one warm session + a supervised restart', not N parallel subprocesses. (3) Subprocess lifecycle / supervision. Spawn via StdioServerParameters(command, args, env) + stdio_client() (async context manager that launches the TS server, wires its stdin/stdout, and yields (read, write) streams). Health is implicit: a crashed child closes stdout -> the read stream EOFs -> in-flight awaits raise. Wrap the connect+session in a supervisor that catches transport closure, performs exponential backoff with jitter, respawns the subprocess, re-runs initialize(), and re-lists tools. Use a circuit breaker (as in ultimate_mcp_client's @retry_with_circuit_breaker) so a server that crashes repeatedly trips open instead of hot-looping. (4) Per-call timeouts + cancellation. The MCP spec says senders SHOULD set per-request timeouts and, on timeout, send a cancellation notification rather than just abandoning the request. Wrap each call_tool in asyncio.wait_for / anyio.fail_after with a per-call timeout (newer SDK ClientSession also accepts read_timeout_seconds). Distinguish transient failures (timeout, broken pipe, EOF -> retry with backoff, possibly after a respawn) from deterministic tool errors (CallToolResult.isError=True / invalid args -> do NOT retry; surface to caller). (5) Clean shutdown. Follow the spec stdio shutdown order: close child stdin, wait for exit, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL. Always tear down with `async with` (or an AsyncExitStack closed in the same owning task, in strict LIFO order) so anyio scopes unwind correctly. (6) Robust stdio parsing. The child MUST only emit valid newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdout and may use stderr for logs; defensively filter/ignore non-JSON noise on stdout (ultimate_mcp_client's RobustStdioSession does exactly this) so a stray TS console.log doesn't corrupt the stream. Net: one supervised, single-task-owned, long-lived ClientSession over stdio, with per-call timeouts+cancellation, backoff+circuit-breaker reconnection, and spec-compliant subprocess teardown.
reference_papers: A Survey of the Model Context Protocol (MCP): Standardizing Context to Enhance Large Language Models (LLMs) (Singh, Ehtesham, Kumar & Talaei Khoei, 2025) - Preprints.org 202504.0245 - primary survey of MCP architecture, JSON-RPC 2.0 client-server design, lifecycle/handshake, transports (stdio + HTTP/SSE), and security considerations
A Survey of AI Agent Protocols (2025) - arxiv:2504.16736 - situates MCP among agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent protocols; useful for transport/lifecycle design trade-offs

ScaleMCP: Dynamic and Auto-Synchronizing Model Context Protocol Tools for LLM Agents (2025) - arxiv:2505.06416 - dynamic discovery/synchronization of MCP tools at scale; relevant to client-side tool-list refresh after reconnect [uncertain - more about tool retrieval than client transport internals]
reference_repos: modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk - Official Python SDK (mcp package, stable v1.27.1 as of May 2026; v2 alpha in progress). Provides ClientSession, StdioServerParameters, stdio_client(); foundation for any client - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk

Dicklesworthstone/ultimate_mcp_client - Most feature-complete async Python MCP client: RobustStdioSession (filters non-JSON-RPC stdout noise, resolves asyncio.Futures by request id), ServerManager with AsyncExitStack-based lifecycle (connect/disconnect/restart), @retry_with_circuit_breaker with exponential backoff. Best architectural reference - https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/ultimate_mcp_client

NousResearch/hermes-agent (tools/mcp_tool.py) - Production long-lived-session pattern: each MCP server runs as a long-lived asyncio Task on a dedicated background event loop, automatic reconnection with exponential backoff (up to 5 retries), per-server timeouts, env-var filtering and credential stripping in errors - https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/tools/mcp_tool.py

langchain-ai/langchain-mcp-adapters - Widely used adapter layer wrapping the mcp client for agent frameworks; good reference for session management and surfaced anyio cancel-scope shutdown issues - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-mcp-adapters
IBM/mcp-context-forge - MCP gateway; issue #258 tracks universal client retry with exponential backoff + jitter + circuit breaker across transports - https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge

openai/openai-agents-python (MCP integration) - Shows reconnect(failed_only=True/False), connect_timeout_seconds, cleanup_timeout_seconds, connect_in_parallel lifecycle tuning - https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python
key_libraries: mcp - Python - >=1.27,<2 (stable 1.27.1, May 2026; pin <2 since v2 stable targets 2026-07-27). Official MCP SDK: ClientSession, StdioServerParameters, mcp.client.stdio.stdio_client(); core of the bridge

anyio - Python - >=4.9 - async runtime the mcp SDK is built on (asyncio/trio backends, task groups, cancel scopes, fail_after for timeouts). Critical to understand for correct session lifecycle (same-task enter/exit of cancel scopes)

asyncio - Python - stdlib (Python 3.10+) - orchestrator's event loop; asyncio.wait_for for per-call timeouts, asyncio.Queue/Future for request multiplexing onto the single session task, asyncio.create_task for the supervisor
pydantic - Python - v2 (pydantic + pydantic-settings, deps of mcp) - typed models for JSON-RPC payloads and tool result parsing (TextContent / structured content)
httpx + httpx-sse - Python - httpx <1.0.0 - only needed if also supporting HTTP/SSE transport; not required for pure stdio bridge [uncertain - optional for stdio-only use]
backoff - Python - >=2.x - decorator-based exponential backoff + full jitter (backoff.full_jitter) for sync and async; clean way to implement transient-failure retry
tenacity - Python - >=8.x - alternative retry library with rich async support, stop/wait/retry-if policies and circuit-breaker-style composition [uncertain - either backoff or tenacity, not both]
uncertain: ScaleMCP relevance to client transport internals (more about tool retrieval/sync than subprocess/JSON-RPC handling)
httpx/httpx-sse necessity for a stdio-only bridge (optional unless HTTP transport is later added)
choice between backoff vs tenacity for retry (project should pick one)
exact ClientSession timeout kwarg name across SDK versions (read_timeout_seconds present in recent versions; verify against pinned mcp version)
